title: super.context() in a static charges the CONTAINING capability, not the base class the checker's type for super names
notes: specification/requirements.mdx, 'Capability Identity': capability identity is nominal; 'Context Access': the receiver must identify the subclass whose key the read records. In a static method, `super.context()` invokes the INHERITED static with `this` still bound to Registry, so the constructor the runtime keys its lookup on is Registry — and `typeof Directory`, which is what the checker gives for `super`, is the one key that read can never have. This case is the odd one of the set: every sibling in the ambiguity family asserts a REFUSAL, and this one asserts a ROW. That is deliberate and it is the only shape that can state it. A row is not directly observable through any corpus expectation, and it is not readable out of the Go fork at all, so the row is put where a rule reads it: the layer provides Directory, and `SMITHERS2101` names what is MISSING. A backend that recorded `[Directory]` — which is what both backends did until 2026-08-26 — would find the layer complete and report nothing at all, so the presence of this diagnostic is the assertion that the row is not Directory. `messageContains` IS the promise here and is not decoration: code and position alone are satisfied by a refusal naming any missing capability, and the entire content of the case is WHICH capability is missing. `Registry` is the smallest fragment that carries it and is a substring of both backends' renderings (`Layer.provide is missing Registry` on the reference, `Layer.provide is missing {Registry}` on the fork), which is why the bare name is declared rather than either sentence — measured on both backends rather than assumed. This is the same use `06-layers/layer-provide-missing-a-capability-an-accessor-introduces` makes of the mechanism. WHAT THIS DELIBERATELY DOES NOT PIN: it does not settle whether `typeof Directory` covers `typeof Registry` under subtyping in general — that is a recorded open residual on both backends, and `requirements.mdx` settles neither `Capability Identity` nor `Context Access` against it. `super` is a narrower and fully decided question: it names a key the read can never have, whatever the answer to the subtyping one turns out to be. Registry adds no member of its own, so the case cannot be passing because the two capabilities have different shapes. VERIFIED LOAD-BEARING, not assumed: mutating the declared fragment from `Registry` to `Directory` turns the case red on BOTH backends with the message diff printed, and the file was restored byte-identically (sha256 3e6e3f4bf52252fb59db44fee568d537ff6236ba6304677959a17a76d7c0da70 before and after).
